## Observed (pm 2026.10.15)

```console
$ pm list --status open --limit 2 --sort priority --format json | jq -c '.items[0]|keys'
["id","status","title","type"]
```

The result is ordered by `priority`, but the brief projection (`id,status,type,title`) leaves the sort key out. The ordering is visible but the value behind it isn't. An agent that asked for priority order and reads `.priority` gets `null` for every row. Then it either re-runs with `--fields id,priority,...` or misreports priorities. That happened in this session: a backlog survey printed `pnull` for every item.

The same applies to `--sort updated_at` / `created_at` / `deadline`.

## Proposal

When `--sort <field>` is given and `--fields` is not, add the sort field to the brief projection. In TOON that is one extra column. Record it in `projection.fields` so the omission receipt stays accurate. An explicit `--fields` stays authoritative.
GH-1481: Agent UX: pm list --sort <field> omits the sort key from the brief projection
GitHub report https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1481. An explicit list sort makes its sort key visible in the implicit brief projection, while explicit requested fields remain authoritative.
Explicit sort fields appear in implicit brief projection and projection.fields; Explicit --fields remains authoritative; SDK and CLI share the projection rule
